subject: periodical cicada
title: These Insects Wait Underground for 17 Years, Then Appear All at Once

scenes.text: Some insects wait underground for exactly 17 years, then all appear at once.
Periodical cicadas spend those years as nymphs, sipping sap from tree roots.
When the soil warms to about 65 degrees Fahrenheit, they surge out. Up to 1.5 million on a single acre.
Why all at once? So many appear that predators can't eat them all.
And why 13 or 17 years? Both are prime numbers, but scientists still aren't sure why.
Seventeen years of waiting. Then one loud summer.

description:
Periodical cicadas spend 13 or 17 years underground, then emerge together, up to 1.5 million per acre.
So many appear at once that predators can't eat them all.
Would you wait 17 years for one loud summer? Tell us below.
